chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:
I wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with some questions, some of them with Ibn Bukayr and some with Abu al-Abbas. So the answer came with his dictation:
You asked about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And for Allah upon the people is a pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to undertake to it a way.'
He means by it the Hajj and the Umrah together, because both of them are obligatory.
And I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And complete the Hajj and the Umrah for Allah.'
He said: He means by their completion, their fulfillment, and abstaining from what the one in Ihram abstains from during them.
And I asked him about the Words of the Exalted: 'the greater Hajj'.
What is meant by 'the greater Hajj'?
So he said: The greater Hajj is the standing at Arafat and the pelting of the Jamarat, and the lesser Hajj is the Umrah.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The one in Ihram (state of consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of the Greater Hajj and Lesser Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imami jurisprudential approach to interpreting Quranic terminology, specifically clarifying that the obligation of 'Hajj' encompasses both the major pilgrimage and Umrah. It further elucidates the concept of 'completing' these rites as not merely performing rituals but maintaining ritual purity and avoiding prohibitions, while distinguishing the 'Greater Hajj' (standing at Arafat) from the 'Lesser Hajj' (Umrah). This reflects the scholarly emphasis on precise ritual execution and the spiritual integrity required during the state of Ihram.
